To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We propose a novel spiking neural network architecture that can learn to solve complex spatio-temporal tasks, such as the MNIST sequence classification task.
we have developed an efficient method for converting gated recurrent neural networks into spiking neural networks.

1) the proposed spiking Long Short-Term Network (SLSTM) achieves state-of-the-art accuracy for the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, 2) the SLSTM is able to learn to perform a variety of tasks, including classification, regression, and reinforcement learning, and 3) the SLSTM can learn to solve tasks that require temporal processing, such as predicting the future based on a sequence of past observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient, biologically plausible and scalable spiking neural networks.
the development of spiking recurrent neural networks for the processing and analysis of sensory information.
the development of spiking neural networks, and their applications in machine learning and cognitive science.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel spiking neural network architecture that can learn and classify time series.
we have developed a novel spiking neural network that achieves state-of-the-art results on a number of benchmarks.
we propose a novel way to gate recurrent networks using spike-based neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

spiking networks can be made more efficient by reducing the amount of information transmitted in the network and that this can be done in a way that is compatible with the biological constraints of the network.
it is possible to implement gated recurrent neural networks with spiking neurons, which can learn to solve tasks that require temporal processing.
the spiking LSTMs are able to learn and generalize better than non-spiking LSTMs.
